extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent representatives/attorneys, and KIPO examiners/staff (users of the Korean Patent Act and Enforcement Rules)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on procedural requirements for representation, calculation and extension of periods, invalidation/ restoration of proceedings, and return of illegitimate documents under the Korean Patent Act and its Enforcement Rules. Covers how deadlines are computed, when extensions/shortenings are allowed, and grounds/procedures for invalidation or returning documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Survival of subagent representation upon representative's death
rubrics_metrics.description: The power of representation of a subagent in a patent-related proceeding shall not be extinguished in case of death of a representative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This follows from applying provisions of the Civil Procedure Act mutatis mutandis to the Patent Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple representatives each independently represent principal
rubrics_metrics.description: Where two or more representatives have been appointed, each of them shall independently represent the principal before KIPO or the Intellectual Property Trial and Appeal Board.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Principle of individual representation applies to acts between appointed representatives; between principal and representative; representative and subagent; principal and subagent; and repeated proceedings by the same representative. Example: where more than two representatives have respectively submitted written amendments in response to a notice of grounds for rejection, all amendments shall be deemed legitimately submitted. Examiner must confirm which specification to examine with reference to confirmation methods (Part 5, Ch.3 §6.3.1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Retroactive effect of ratified proceedings by unauthorized or incapacitated persons
rubrics_metrics.description: Proceedings conducted by a person who lacks legal capacity, the power of legal representation, or necessary authorization shall have retroactive effect to the time of performance if ratified by the principal when the principal has gained legal capacity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to actions by incompetents or unauthorized agents once legitimately ratified by the principal (e.g., a minor who later reaches age 19).

rubrics_metrics.name: Joint conduct of proceedings by multiple parties and common representative rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Where more than two parties jointly conduct a patent-related proceeding, each represents them all except for actions that could incur disadvantages to other parties; if more-than-two parties appoint a common representative and notify KIPO, only the common representative can conduct the proceeding (multiple common representatives may be appointed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A common representative must submit evidential documents proving appointment and attach a power of attorney when conducting proceedings by an agent. Even a common representative cannot conduct certain acts under Article 11(1) without special powers from multiple parties; if conducted without special power, KIPO will request amendment and may invalidate the proceeding if deficiencies are not addressed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partial appointment of representative
rubrics_metrics.description: When only some parties appoint a representative, the appointed representative can conduct the patent-related proceeding on behalf of all parties involved, but must conduct the Article 11(1) specified proceedings jointly with other parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a common representative does not represent all applicants, the representative's name must be indicated as that applicant's representative in the application form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calculation of periods — first day and midnight rule
rubrics_metrics.description: The first day of a period shall not be counted; provided, however, that the foregoing shall not apply where a period commences at midnight (i.e., then the first day is counted).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is Article 14(1) of the Patent Act and is reinforced in the calculation examples: if a notice is delivered at midnight the computation begins that day; otherwise the first counted day is the day after transmittal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calculation of periods expressed in months or years
rubrics_metrics.description: If a period is expressed in months or years, it shall be counted according to the calendar; when the starting day does not fall on the beginning of a month/year, the period expires on the day before the corresponding date in the last month/year; if there is no corresponding day in the last month, the period expires on the last day of that month.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples and diagrams illustrate expirations (e.g., period starting 12/30 with 2-month designated period expires on 2/28).

rubrics_metrics.name: Holiday rule for expiration dates
rubrics_metrics.description: If the last day of a period for performing a patent-related proceeding falls on an official holiday (including designated Workers' Day and Saturdays), the period shall expire on the next working day.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: this holiday-extension rule does not apply to certain patent-unrelated statutory periods (e.g., domestic priority deemed-withdrawal or patent term expiration). Example: if an amendment expiration falls on Lunar New Year (holiday) and the following day is Sunday, the amendment period expires on the next working day (illustrated using case law No. 90 Hu 1680).

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary calculation governed by Patent Act Article 14; Civil Act supplementary
rubrics_metrics.description: Periods are calculated primarily according to Article 14 of the Patent Act; Article 155 of the Civil Act applies supplementarily except for special cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The methods are divided into natural calculation (precise, inconvenient) and calendar calculation (somewhat imprecise, convenient). Guidance and examples show how to apply the rules in practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic submission network glitch rule
rubrics_metrics.description: If a person attempted to submit electronic documents through a computerized network but failed to deliver them within the period because of a network glitch, the period shall mature on the following day when the glitch has been removed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Network glitch includes failure of the computerized network and malfunction of computers or relevant devices used in KIPO. If KIPO has previously notified network glitches in advance, they are not deemed glitches. Refer to Enforcement Rules Article 9(4) and the Announcement of Term Extension for Failure of Computerized Network for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of Article 15 when period expires on holiday and extension counting
rubrics_metrics.description: When a period is expired pursuant to Article 15 and the last day falls on a public holiday, the initial period matures on that public holiday and any extension of the period is counted from the day after the expiration day of the period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When multiple extensions are requested, each extension period shall be calculated in the same manner. Detailed timeline examples demonstrate computation across month boundaries and holiday effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commissioner/judge/examiner power to extend or shorten designated periods
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commissioner of KIPO, President of the Trial and Appeal Board, presiding administrative patent judge, or an examiner may, upon request or ex officio, shorten or extend periods set for carrying out patent-related proceedings; Commissioner may extend specific statutory petition-for-trial periods once by up to 30 days with possible additional allowances for remote areas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When shortening/extending, authorities must ensure interests of relevant parties are not unfairly infringed. Presiding judges may change deadlines upon request or ex officio.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory periods vs designated periods
rubrics_metrics.description: Statutory periods are those defined in the Patent Act or Orders under it; designated periods are those set by KIPO officials (Commissioner, President, judges, examiners) for persons filing applications or performing proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists of common statutory and designated periods related to examination (e.g., priority claim periods, request for examination, time for laying open application, appeal periods, amendment periods) are provided to distinguish types and applicable rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension of statutory periods (limited allowance)
rubrics_metrics.description: A statutory period for filing a petition for trial under Article 132(17) may be extended only once by up to 30 days; persons in areas with poor transportation may receive additional extensions as prescribed by Ordinance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: President of the Trial and Appeal Board (Trial Policy Division) determines whether statutory extension requirements are met and whether to accept the request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension of substantive examination designated periods — general acceptance rule
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for extension of a designated substantive-examination period can be filed for one month each time or for more than two months at once; requests for less than one month are deemed one month. A request is deemed accepted when submitted, except for the submission period for written argument.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An examiner may disapprove extensions that unlawfully infringe interests of others and may approve only the necessary time after a warning of disapproval for the rest. If fees for extension aren't paid, examiner will order amendment; payments made within designated period render the request legitimate; unpaid fees by deadline invalidate the request. If extension request is submitted after expiration, examiner will allow explanation and return the request and return fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension of submission period for written argument — time limits and allowed reasons
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for extension of the submission period for a written argument is deemed accepted when submitted if the desired extension expiration is within four months from the original expiration. If the allowed window has elapsed, an examiner will consider reasons and may approve only within the allowed window.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permissible reasons include: (①) appointing/changing representative within one month before expiration; (②) change/addition of applicant within one month; (③) receipt/submission of foreign office examination results within two months before expiration; (④) written-argument delivery delay over one month; (⑤) earlier/subsequent application pending in trial/lawsuit; (⑥) need for tests and analysis relating to grounds for rejection; (⑦) other inevitable necessity. Requests related to third-party-filed applications are generally disapproved even if they correspond to reasons ①–⑤. Examiners may require explanations for additional extension requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension and approval rules for formalities-examination designated periods
rubrics_metrics.description: The amendment (formalities) period under Article 46 may be extended in one-month increments or more; requested periods less than one month are deemed one month. The total period allowed for extension is four months (subject to extra allowances for international national-phase filings).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the total requested extension does not exceed four months and fees are paid, the request is deemed approved upon submission. If a four-month extension is granted, the examiner must state in writing that 'any further extension of the period shall not be allowed' and will disapprove further requests. Late-submitted extension requests are treated like substantive extensions: applicant given chance to explain and fees returned if request not approved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shortening designated periods upon request
rubrics_metrics.description: When a designated period for conducting a proceeding has been set, the period can be shortened upon request. When a request or an amendment indicating shortening is submitted, the designated period is deemed expired on the submission day and the examiner shall carry out the examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This mechanism allows applicants to accelerate examination by formally requesting a shorter period or filing an amendment indicating the desire to shorten the period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order to amend and grounds for ordering amendment (Article 46)
rubrics_metrics.description: KIPO Commissioner or President of the Trial and Appeal Board shall order a person to amend a patent-related proceeding within a specified period where: (1) violations of Article 3(1) or 6 occur; (2) violation of any formality specified in the Act or Orders; or (3) failure to pay any fee required under Article 82.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upon receipt of such an order, the person may submit an argument on the order during the specified period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invalidation of proceeding for failure to amend (Article 16)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a person ordered to amend under Article 46 fails to do so within the specified period, KIPO Commissioner or President of the Trial and Appeal Board may invalidate the patent-related proceeding. If the failure to amend was due to inability to pay certain fees for requesting examination, the amendment to the specification may be invalidated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invalidation may be revoked if failure to amend was due to a cause not attributable to the person and a request to revoke is received within two months after that cause ceases, provided one year has not elapsed since expiration of the specified period. When invalidation or revocation occurs, notice shall be given to the person ordered to amend.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subsequent completion of proceeding where failure due to non-attributable cause (Article 17)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a person failed to complete a proceeding within the period due to a cause not attributable to them, they may subsequently complete the proceeding within two months after the cause ceases to exist (except where one year has passed since expiration). Applies to certain petition-for-trial and retrial filing periods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifically listed: (1) filing a petition for trial under Article 132-17; (2) filing petition for retrial under Article 180(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Restoration of patent application after withdrawal or final rejection (Article 67-3)
rubrics_metrics.description: If an application was withdrawn or a rejection became final due to failure to comply with time limits because of a cause not attributable to the applicant, the applicant may request examination or re-examination within two months from the date the cause ceases to exist, unless one year has elapsed since expiry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If such request is filed pursuant to paragraph (1), the application shall be deemed not to have been withdrawn or the decision not to have become final and conclusive (notwithstanding Article 59(5)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Return of illegitimate application documents (Enforcement Rules Article 11) — list of grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: KIPO or the President of the Trial and Appeal Board shall not deem application documents legitimate (and shall return them) where they fall under enumerated grounds, such as: violation of Enforcement Rules Article 2 (improper form), unclear application/document type, missing name/applicant code/address, not written in Korean, specification missing (including description), specification attached but missing claims when amendment period elapsed, applicant lacks domicile/place of business in Korea (except registered patent administrator), documents not submitted within designated period, extension requests for non-extendable periods, extension requests submitted after applicable expiration, documents submitted after termination of proceeding, documents submitted by person not entitled, unclear required ancillary forms, electronic submissions not using KIPO software or in unprocessable electronic format, and other listed subparagraphs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each enumerated ground includes procedural consequences (return/invalidity). For electronic submissions, KIPO-provided software/format must be used; otherwise the electronic document may be unprocessable and thus illegitimate. Fees or other formal requirements must be met; some specific subparagraphs (e.g., 5-2 re: missing claims) reference elapsed amendment periods.
